settings.question: Do you deliver?
settings.answer: Yes! We have a full-time delivery truck to bring your order right to your front door/loading dock/location.

settings.question: Where do you deliver to?
settings.answer: We deliver throughout Niagara and the GTA. For orders to be delivered outside of this area we are happy to quote shipping with your order.

settings.answer: No, however shipping is free on orders over $300 in the Niagara Region or on orders over $500 in the Hamilton/Toronto area. Under these minimums, delivery charges of $9.90 and $14.90 apply respectively. For the rest of Ontario, a $600 order minimum applies for free shipping.

settings.answer: Absolutely! Our showroom is located at 7 Neilson Ave, St.Catharines ON. Our online shop is also open to the public however we do not currently accept payment online. Please provide your contact number with your order and a member of our staff will contact you to co-ordinate payment and shipping.

settings.question: How do I strip and refinish my VCT?
settings.answer: We made a step by step video tutorial on refinishing VCT that is up on our youtube. Check it out HERE. When you’re ready to start the process, let us know and one of our knowledgeable staff members will be happy to help you with any questions you may have.

settings.question: How do I know I’m using the right product?
settings.answer: If you’re ever unsure if the product you’re thinking of using for a job is the right one, or if you’re concerned about interactions between different chemicals, please allow one of our knowledgeable members of staff assist you. Safety first!

settings.question: How do I pick the right machine for my building?
settings.answer: Choosing the correct machine for your facility depends on several factors- usage, area, storage, budget etc. The first step is to decide what you want to accomplish with your new machine (scrubbing, burnishing, polishing etc), the second step is to have a professional assessment of your facility’s needs. We have several experts who, like a good tailor, will help you find the perfect fit.

settings.question: How do I get rid of urine smell?
settings.answer: Once the initial mess has been ‘cleaned’ it is common for an odour to linger on. The easiest and most effective method to defeat biological odours like urine, is to use a biological. We have a specially formulated product (UCT) which contains bacteria that breakdown and digest residual urine on the cellular level so it can’t make that horrible smell anymore. Safe to use on most water safe surfaces, contact us for specific use instructions.

settings.question: Will you service my machine?
settings.answer: We have an experienced service tech who is available to do in-house service/repairs on most commercial vacuums, floor machines and extractors. When you purchase large equipment from us, we have optional preventative maintenance (PM) service you can sign up for to keep your machine working at its best.

settings.question: Do I have to bring my machine in to your shop for service?
settings.answer: It is generally better to bring your machine into our shop for repair if possible. For some larger floor machines which moving to our shop would be too difficult, we offer an on-site repair service. We also offer a pickup service to customers with an account with us.

settings.question: I’m opening a new store and need my dishwasher set up.
settings.answer: We have a trained technician who can set up your dishwasher, so you get optimal results every time. We also offer dishwashers for rent, lease or to buy. Contact us for a quote.

settings.question: I want to make my building maintenance more efficient, any advice?
settings.answer: We offer on-site assessment! We’ll come to you and assess your building or business and suggest ways/products to optimize efficiency and costs for maintenance.

settings.question: How do I choose a floor finish?
settings.answer:
Start with the floor material, traffic level and the appearance you want. Match the finish to the substrate and consider how often your team can maintain it.

Choose the Right Floor Finish · p. 1

settings.question: When is mopping enough?
settings.answer:
Mopping is useful for daily maintenance, loose dirt, footprints and light spills. Embedded grime or heavy buildup can require scrubbing.

Scrubbing vs. Mopping Floors · p. 1

settings.question: What does burnishing do?
settings.answer:
Burnishing smooths the top layer of floor finish to restore gloss and reduce light scuffs. Pad selection depends on the finish and the equipment.

Choosing the Right Pad for Floor Finish Restoration · p. 1

settings.question: What is Commercial Floor Finish?
settings.answer: A durable acrylic or polymer coating applied over sealed floors (VCT, terrazzo, concrete) to protect the surface and create a glossy, slip-resistant wear layer.

settings.question: How is floor finish different from wax?
settings.answer: Modern "finish" is typically a polymer/acrylic emulsion, not true wax — it's more durable, dries harder, and holds up better to foot traffic and machine buffing.

settings.question: How often should floors be refinished?
settings.answer: Depends on traffic: high-traffic commercial areas often need a full strip-and-refinish every 6–24 months, with spray buffing or recoating in between.

settings.question: What's the difference between recoating and stripping?
settings.answer: Recoating adds a fresh finish layer over existing coats (routine maintenance); stripping removes all old finish down to the sealer before reapplying (needed when buildup, yellowing, or damage occurs).

settings.question: How many coats of finish should be applied?
settings.answer:
Typically, 3–5 thin coats, allowing proper dry time between each, rather than fewer thick coats (which crack and haze).

Follow the rule of 100 plus 1.

If your floor finish has 20% solids you can apply 6 coats 20% x 5= 100 plus one extra coat)

If your floor finish has 24% solids you can apply 5 coats 24% x 4= 96 plus one extra coat)

settings.question: How long does finish need to dry/cure between coats?
settings.answer: Usually 30–45 minutes between coats depending on humidity/temperature; full cure can take 24–72 hours before heavy traffic.

settings.question: Can floors be used right after refinishing?
settings.answer: Light foot traffic is often fine after a few hours, preferably 24 hours for 95% Curing. Furniture and heavy equipment should be kept off until fully cured.

settings.question: What's the difference between high-solids and standard finish?
settings.answer: High-solids finish has more polymer content per coat, meaning fewer coats needed for the same durability and gloss.

settings.question: Should I use a low-maintenance or daily-maintenance floor finish?
settings.answer: In this case it is all about time. If you have equipment and time to maintain your floor 3-7 times per week and you want the results. Have at it!

settings.question: Do I need a different finish for VCT vs. concrete vs. wood?
settings.answer: Yes — finishes are formulated for specific substrates; using the wrong type can cause poor adhesion or premature wear.

settings.question: What does "high-traffic" or "extended durability" finish mean?
settings.answer: These formulas contain higher cross-linking polymers designed to resist scuffing and black heel marks in busy areas like lobbies and hallways.

settings.question: Why is my floor finish turning yellow?
settings.answer: Common causes: UV exposure, ammonia-based cleaners breaking down the finish, or too many buildup layers without stripping.

settings.question: Why does the floor look hazy or streaky after finishing?
settings.answer: Usually applicator/mop contamination, finish applied too thick, or poor floor prep (residue from old stripper).

settings.question: What causes black marks and scuffing?
settings.answer: Rubber-soled shoes and cart wheels; can be minimized with a more durable finish or regular burnishing.

settings.question: How do I remove floor finish buildup?
settings.answer: A commercial-grade stripper matched to the finish type, followed by a neutral rinse before recoating.

settings.question: What cleaners are safe on finished floors?
settings.answer: Neutral pH cleaners only — avoid ammonia, bleach, or acidic cleaners, which degrade finish over time.

settings.question: What does "stripping" a floor mean?
settings.answer: Using a chemical stripper to fully dissolve and remove old layers of finish down to the bare sealer or substrate, rather than just adding another coat on top.

settings.question: How is stripping different from deep scrubbing?
settings.answer: Deep cleaning removes surface dirt; stripping chemically breaks down the finish itself so it can be mopped/wet-vacuumed away.

settings.question: How do I know when a floor needs to be stripped vs. just recoated?
settings.answer: Signs include yellowing, heavy buildup, embedded dirt/black marks that won't buff out, uneven gloss, or finish that's cracking/peeling.

settings.question: What's the basic step-by-step for stripping a floor?
settings.answer: Sweep/dust mop, apply stripper solution, let it dwell, agitate with a low-speed buffer or scrub pad, wet-vacuum or mop up the residue, rinse, then let dry before resealing/refinishing.

settings.question: How long should stripper dwell before scrubbing?
settings.answer: Typically, 5–15 minutes depending on the product and finish buildup — it should stay wet the whole time, so re-wetting may be needed in warm/dry conditions.

settings.question: Can floor stripper become ineffective?
settings.answer: Yes, Stripper is not what carries your floor finish after stripping. Sometimes just adding some room temperature water to the floor while your stripping can stretch a stripper to improve end results.

settings.question: Do I need to rinse after stripping?
settings.answer: Yes — a neutral rinse is essential to remove residual stripper/finish sludge; leftover residue causes poor adhesion of the new finish.

settings.question: How long should a floor dry before applying new finish?
settings.answer: Usually a minimum of 30–60 minutes, but it must be fully dry (no damp spots) — humidity and airflow affect this.

settings.question: What's the difference between a "no-rinse" and standard stripper?
settings.answer: No-rinse strippers are formulated to leave less residue, saving a step, but still often benefit from at least a light rinse on heavy buildup jobs.

settings.question: What equipment do I need to strip a floor?
settings.answer: Low-speed buffer with a stripping pad, wet vacuum, mop buckets, scraper for edges/corners, and PPE (gloves, eye protection).

settings.question: Can I use the same stripper on any type of floor finish?
settings.answer: Not always — stripper strength and formulation should match the finish type and substrate (VCT, terrazzo, wood needs specific low-moisture strippers). Consult with your supplier support team.

settings.question: Are strippers safe on all floor types?
settings.answer: No — wood, some stone, and certain specialty floors can be damaged by standard strippers; always check compatibility first.

settings.question: Why is finish still visible after stripping?
settings.answer: Usually insufficient dwell time, stripper drying out before agitation, or too few passes with the buffer/scrub pad — may need a second application.

settings.question: Why does the floor feel tacky or sticky after stripping?
settings.answer: Incomplete rinsing, leaving stripper/finish residue behind — re-rinse until water runs clear.

settings.question: What causes dull spots after refinishing a stripped floor?
settings.answer: Usually residue left in low spots/edges, or finish applied over an area that wasn't fully dry.

settings.question: How do I handle edges and corners a buffer can't reach?
settings.answer: Hand-scrub with a stripping pad (Doodle Bug) or scraper, or use an edger attachment, then wet-vac separately.
